documents.abstract: Contrastive pretraining may reduce the labelled data required for detector classification.

chunks.title: Convolutional Networks for Gravitational-Wave Detection
chunks.text: The study uses a convolutional neural network to classify detector time-series windows. The model learns local waveform features directly from whitened strain data.

chunks.title: Convolutional Networks for Gravitational-Wave Detection
chunks.text: The convolutional model reported a 14% sensitivity improvement over the matched-filter baseline on the simulated test set. Performance fell when the labelled training set was small.

chunks.title: Bayesian and Matched-Filter Baselines
chunks.text: Bayesian inference and matched filtering use waveform templates to estimate signal probabilities. These baselines provide calibrated uncertainty estimates and transparent parameter assumptions.

chunks.title: Bayesian and Matched-Filter Baselines
chunks.text: The authors report that template mismatch can reduce matched-filter recall for unexpected signal morphologies. They argue that template-based methods remain preferable when calibrated uncertainty is required.

chunks.title: Benchmarking Detection Models on Small Datasets
chunks.text: On the smallest labelled dataset, the convolutional model improved recall by 10% while the transformer improved recall by 5%. The transformer required more examples before its attention layers became stable.

chunks.title: Benchmarking Detection Models on Small Datasets
chunks.text: Reported gains are not directly comparable across noise simulations and thresholds. The benchmark recommends reporting recall, false-alarm rate, training set size, and confidence intervals together.

chunks.title: Attention Models for Detector Time Series
chunks.text: The transformer uses self-attention over detector time series to model long-range waveform context. It was trained on a large simulated dataset with augmented noise.

chunks.title: Attention Models for Detector Time Series
chunks.text: On the large simulated dataset, the attention model achieved a 22% improvement in detection sensitivity. It did not outperform the convolutional model on the smallest labelled split.

chunks.title: Attention Models for Detector Time Series
chunks.text: Attention models have high memory costs and depend on large training sets. The authors caution that simulated-data gains may not transfer unchanged to nonstationary detector noise.

chunks.title: A Review of Machine Learning in Gravitational-Wave Searches
chunks.text: Between 2021 and 2025, published work shifted from convolutional classifiers toward attention and representation-learning approaches. The review attributes this change to larger simulations and interest in long-range context.

chunks.title: A Review of Machine Learning in Gravitational-Wave Searches
chunks.text: Authors disagree about whether simulated benchmark improvements demonstrate readiness for detector operations. Some prioritise sensitivity gains, whereas others prioritise uncertainty calibration and robustness to changing noise.

chunks.title: Preliminary Contrastive Detector Representation
chunks.text: Contrastive pretraining may reduce the labelled data required for detector classification.
